solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: CIC? I'm apt for training around him, combining characteristics

indicators.note: letters put through training are drilled into a new formation
the reworked letters sit on either side of another word, enclosing it

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A commanding officer reckons he is fit to train a man with mixed qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: CIC looks like an abbreviation for commander-in-chief, but it is simply three letters of anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology the word describes reproduction by fusion of two gametes, which merges the inherited traits of both parents.

clue.text: Right hand used in Pompeian artwork (not left)? unidentified material

indicators.note: something used in a work is placed inside it
'not left' tells us the artwork must go without that letter

blocks.note: Pompeii is famous for its wall paintings
standard abbreviation, removed from the painting
standard abbreviation for right hand

explanation.surface: A question about a painting in Pompeii, made using the right hand without the left, and what it was made of.
explanation.walkthrough: The wall painting loses its final letter and takes the right-hand abbreviation into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrha was the substance of prized Roman murrhine vases; nobody now knows exactly what mineral it was, hence unidentified.

clue.text: There's a smell endlessly round mobile lat or … this?

definitions.text: There's a smell endlessly round mobile lat or … this?

indicators.note: without its end, the word for a smell loses its final letter
something mobile moves about, so these letters move into a new order
one part wraps round the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: pooh is the exclamation at a bad smell; it loses its end
letters taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Is a portable latrine, with its lingering odour, what the clue describes?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a lat (latrine) that is mobile, with a smell about it. Portaloo is a British brand name for a portable toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Portaloo is a portable toilet cabin, the kind of mobile latrine notorious for its odour.

clue.text: Fine porcelain greeting oriental Buddhist

blocks.note: an informal greeting
Zen is a Japanese school of Buddhism, used here as a person or form

explanation.surface: A delicate china piece greets a Buddhist from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Hizen is a Japanese ware named after the province where Arita and Imari porcelain was made.

clue.text: Opossum some damaged grabbing limb

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of their original shape
the rearranged word holds another inside it as if clutching it

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: An injured opossum seizes something by a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmose is a small South American mouse opossum, a member of that marsupial family.

clue.text: By the sound of it you are in pub to prepare for tea (probably not!)

indicators.note: we want letters that match what is heard, not the spelling
one part is placed inside the other

blocks.note: text-speak spelling that sounds the same
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone at the pub is told to get ready for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: To put something in an urn sounds like tea-making, but the urn here holds ashes, hence 'probably not!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing something in an urn is also what is done when making tea for a crowd, the joke the setter exploits.

clue.text: Azedders battling for preferment? It's an old conspiracy

blocks.note: the solvers vying in Azed's monthly clue-writing contest: the competition crowd, shortened to two words

explanation.surface: Azed solvers jostling for a prize are said to be part of a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Azedders are regular solvers of this puzzle; those who enter the monthly competition are the competition (comp) lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Complot is an archaic word for a plot or conspiracy, from French.

clue.text: Singers may hum it contralaterally in part

indicators.note: only part of the following word is wanted, a run of its letters

blocks.note: the run sits inside this long word

explanation.surface: A choir may hum something on opposite sides, partly.
explanation.walkthrough: Contralaterally means on the opposite side of the body; it is only the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a wordless refrain sung or hummed in place of lyrics.

clue.text: Working at clothiers? Ah, toil with such snips maybe

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being turned into something else
the rearranged letters equal one phrase together with 'such' a word, so that phrase is taken away to leave it

blocks.note: the whole fodder, rearranged
these letters are part of the rearrangement and are taken out

explanation.surface: Working in a tailor's shop, toiling with scissor snips.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the letters of 'at clothiers' make 'Ah, toil' plus the answer. Snips look like scissor cuts at the clothiers but are sure bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is British slang for a sure thing or bargain, and certs, short for certainties, are sure winners.

clue.text: Spot leaders taking shelter in dozy- looking lot

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within

blocks.note: to spot is to spy
the lee is the sheltered side
heads are leaders

explanation.surface: Leaders seen taking cover among a drowsy-looking crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot leaders' reads as one idea but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepyheads are drowsy people, so a group of them is a dozy-looking bunch.

clue.text: Sandy's stated condition for hairstyle

blocks.note: quo' is the Scots form of quoth (said); Sandy is a stock Scotsman
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A Scot sets out his terms for a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy, short for Alexander, is the crossword's typical Scot, so his speech is in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoif is a variant of coif, a close-fitting cap or a way of arranging the hair.

clue.text: Dodgy old doctor, mercurial? I'll go for one twice

indicators.note: to go for is to stand in place of, swapping one letter for another
the swap happens two times, at every occurrence of the letter

blocks.note: quicksilver is mercury, and as an adjective means mercurial
the letter I is the one being replaced
a means one; it replaces each of the two Is

explanation.surface: A shifty old doctor wonders if he is volatile and will swap one for another twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' tells us both Is in the mercurial word are swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A quacksalver is an archaic term for a charlatan or quack who sells bogus salves and remedies.

clue.text: Old Scandinavian line, one for fastening nets

blocks.note: Norse was the language of medieval Scandinavia
standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A Viking line used to secure fishing nets.
explanation.definitionFit: A norsel is a short cord tied to a fishing net to fasten it to a rope.

clue.text: Autumn time? strange breeze featuring in fringes thereof

indicators.note: something featuring in another appears within it

blocks.note: thereof points back to breeze; its fringes are its first and last letters
rum means odd in British slang
a breeze is a light movement of air

explanation.surface: Is autumn the time for an odd wind blowing at the edges?
explanation.walkthrough: 'breeze' does double work: it gives a piece and its own edges supply the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Brumaire was the second month of the French Revolutionary calendar, running from late October to late November.

clue.text: A king swathes heart of château in 'lumpy' coating

indicators.note: to swathe is to wrap round, enclosing whatever is inside
the heart of something is its centre, so only the central letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
rex is Latin for king
the central letter of the French word

explanation.surface: A monarch wraps up the inner rooms of a French castle in rough plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Artex is a British brand of textured plaster for walls and ceilings, popular in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Artex is a textured decorative finish whose swirled, uneven surface makes it a lumpy coating.

clue.text: Serving prince, deceased

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for prince
the late king means the dead king

explanation.surface: Waiting on a royal who has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' looks like a verb, but here it is a noun: a helping of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of food is one helping or portion, so it is a serving.

clue.text: Carol and Jackie, maybe, offspring

blocks.note: Jackie Chan is the martial-arts film star
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Carol and Jackie, perhaps, with their children.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol and Jackie read as two first names; Carol is really a song, and Jackie stands for a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanson is a French song, and a carol is likewise a song, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Rusty flex around was annoying

indicators.note: one word goes around another, enclosing it

blocks.note: a flex is an electric cord
to ride someone is to harass or nag them

explanation.surface: An old rusty cable wrapped around something was irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Flex is the British word for an electric cable on an appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Corroded metal has been eaten away chemically, as rust does to iron.

clue.text: Spiritual leader, one caught in heated criticism, making comeback

indicators.note: something caught in another is trapped inside it
coming back means travelling the opposite way, so read right to left

blocks.note: flak is fierce criticism
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A religious leader caught out by fierce criticism stages a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A kalif, more often spelt caliph, is the religious and civil head of a Muslim community.

clue.text: One strolling pathway in warm coating

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the other

blocks.note: an animal's fur keeps it warm
a lane is a narrow path

explanation.surface: Someone walks along a path in a warm coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flâneur is an idle stroller or man about town, from the French verb to saunter.

clue.text: What was dizzying? Appalling cost? well I never!

indicators.note: something appalling is in a dreadful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
oh my is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A dizzying bill prompts the cry, what a shocking price!
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' marks the definition as an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotomy is an obsolete term for dizziness with dimness of sight, the giddy feeling of vertigo.

clue.text: Crop in conveyance moved slowly

blocks.note: a bird's crop is its craw
someone led is in the course of being conducted or conveyed

explanation.surface: A harvest is carried in a vehicle at a snail's pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' looks like a harvest but is the pouch in a bird's gullet; 'conveyance' looks like a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To crawl is to creep along slowly, so crawled is the past tense of going at a slow pace.

clue.text: Sore lip after battering? It gives the game away!

indicators.note: a battering knocks things out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A boxer's swollen lip after a pounding shows he lost the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoiler reveals a plot twist or result in advance, letting the secret out.

clue.text: Link in bracelet or chain

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word, the middle one and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A link in a piece of jewellery, a bracelet or a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Link' seems to mean a chain link; in old usage it is a torch carried to light the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A link was a torch of pitch and tow once carried by link-boys to light pedestrians through dark streets.

clue.text: Measure of old grain a client ordered I shifted

indicators.note: a letter that is shifted is moved out of the way, taken away
letters put in order are arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A customer once ordered grain by a certain measure and the speaker moved it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cental is a weight of a hundred pounds, formerly used in Britain for trading grain.

clue.text: What palmist may read that's put on

blocks.note: first meaning: a fleshy rise on the palm
second meaning: to stage a show or exhibition

explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' suggests pretence, but here it means staging something.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry reads the raised pads of the hand, called mounts, and to mount a play is to stage it.

clue.text: Peak like this may be seen in Old Man

indicators.note: something seen in another is placed within it

blocks.note: vir is Latin, the old language, for man
so means in this way

explanation.surface: A summit shaped like this may be spotted on the Old Man, the Lake District fell above Coniston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' signals Latin, the old language, and 'Peak' is the brim of a cap, not a mountain top.
explanation.definitionFit: The visor of a cap is its projecting front brim, also called the peak.

clue.text: Old horse with pedigree? See harness frame

blocks.note: a pad was an old word for an easy-paced riding horse
a family tree records a pedigree

explanation.surface: A thoroughbred nag of former times is shown with its tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad-tree is the wooden or metal frame of a harness saddle that the pad is built on.

clue.text: Cloak from past enveloping everything

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap something up inside

blocks.note: pa. is the dictionary abbreviation for past
all means everything

explanation.surface: A cloak from long ago wraps up everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A palla was the long rectangular mantle worn by women in ancient Rome.

clue.text: What's left in loose earth raised in a fine stream once

definitions.note: the answer is a verb, flowed in a fine stream; the clue gives the manner only

indicators.note: one part is placed inside the other
in a down entry, raising a word lifts it so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for left
dirt is soil

explanation.surface: Something left in raised soil once trickled away in a thin stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Trild is the Spenserian past tense of trill, to trickle or flow in a small stream.

clue.text: Access via code? observe trap

blocks.note: lo means look or behold
a gin is a snare for animals

explanation.surface: Gaining entry with a password: watch out for the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A login is the process of entering a computer system, usually with a username and password.

clue.text: Chemical combination? page includes it for support

indicators.note: the support word is said to be one word holding the answer inside, so that outer word is stripped away

blocks.note: patronage is backing or support
taken as written; its letters wrap round the answer

explanation.surface: A chemical compound: the page includes it as backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works in reverse: the answer placed inside page makes patronage, so stripping page from patronage leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trona is a natural mineral compound of sodium carbonate and bicarbonate, a chemical combination of salts.

clue.text: Forceps lulls Eva being operated on

indicators.note: what is operated on gets cut up and reworked, so the letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Surgical tongs soothe a patient called Eva during her operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulsella is a surgical forceps with hooked or toothed jaws for gripping tissue.

clue.text: Give animation to wild ones, duly free of curbs?

indicators.note: wild letters run free, out of their order
curbs are borders, so the word loses its edges and keeps its interior

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the inner letters of the word

explanation.surface: Inspiring the wild ones who have been properly freed from restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curbs' sounds like restraints; here a curb is an edge, as of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensoul is to infuse with a soul, giving life or spirit to something.

clue.text: Hoppers emptied fields bagging ale's components

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving just its outside letters
a word broken into components can be put back together in a new order
to bag is to put something inside a bag, enclosing it

blocks.note: first and last letters only
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Insects leap across empty fields, catching what makes beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleas are tiny jumping insects, famed for their huge leaps, so they are hoppers.

clue.text: A fib

blocks.note: surface reading: the plain dictionary meaning, a small lie
setter's reading: this is the puzzle's competition entry, which solvers were invited to clue themselves, so no wordplay is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was Azed's clue-writing competition word: the printed clue is only the definition, and solvers had to supply their own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a jocular colloquialism for a petty lie or piece of nonsense.
